thread:
alix: Heads up — after the RFC merge, we need a plan for router-side throttles + fairness when a single tenant spikes. Current dedicated -> fallback behavior is too manual. Thoughts on a generic middleware?

mira: +1. We should avoid per-request blocking in the runtime process. Prefer an external admission controller that signals tokens/backpressure.

devon: What about a two-layer approach: 1) fast local token-bucket per-connection for latency SLOs, 2) centralized scheduler for fairness/quotas that returns short-lived lease tokens.

sam: central scheduler needs to be extremely fast. If leases take 5ms, we lose the latency profile. Can we do coarse-grained leases (e.g., per-100ms window) to amortize?

alix: Coarse windows sound right. Also need graceful degradation paths: if scheduler unreachable, runtime should fall back to per-customer rate caps with conservative defaults.

jaime: +1 on fallback. For abuse prevention we should integrate signals from the anomaly detector (eng-ml) to adjust weights in the scheduler in near real-time. That detector already emits an L0 flag.

mira: Implementation sketch: Scheduler in front of pool, stores tokens in Redis with sharded keys. Leases are just incremented counters with CAS semantics. Worker checks local cache for lease id -> proceed. If no lease, queue briefly (10-20ms) then reject 429.

devon: Redis might be fine for counters, but CAS under 100k TPS could be a bottleneck. Consider a hybrid: Redis for long-term quotas, a ring-buffer service (golang) for millisecond leases.

sam: Also consider token-chaining for streaming requests (long-lived) — we should allow a streaming call to renew its lease cheaply (local touch) rather than re-acquire from scheduler for every token.

alix: Good call. Lease renewal API: POST /lease/renew {lease_id, customer, seq} -> returns success/expiry. Keep renewals idempotent.

ops-bot: deploy: canary rollout scheduled for quota-router v0.1 to dedicated-staging at 2026-02-10T18:00Z :rocket:

jaime: For fairness policies we should support weighted fairness + emergency priority escalation for SRE/customer incidents. Policy syntax idea: 
```
policy {
  tenant_weight: 1.0
  emergency_priority: false
  burst_allowance: 100
}
```

mira: Let's avoid too many knobs in the first iteration. Deliver: per-tenant weight, window-size, and emergency switch. Extra fields can be added later.

devon: Migration plan: 1) route a subset of tenants to router v0.1 with conservative defaults, 2) enable renewals for streaming, 3) enable ML-signal integration, 4) flip default routing. We should log sampling traces for every rejected request.

sam: Metrics to track: per-tenant reject-rate, average wait-time at admission, lease-allocation latency P50/P95, renew-failures, ML-score adjustments. We need dashboards and alert thresholds before broad rollout.

alix: Agree. Action items: @mira draft short RFC follow-up with API shapes + fallback behavior, @devon prototype ring-buffer lease service, @jaime wire up ML flag integration and ops-bot canary. I'll coordinate the rollout timeline.

mira: Will have draft by EOD Friday.

devon: I'll spike the ring-buffer prototype Wednesday.

jaime: I'll add metric names to the observability plan and create initial dashboards in Grafana.

sam: If anyone wants to discuss performance numbers, ping me — I can run microbenchmarks on the lease paths.

alix: thanks all. marking this thread as follow-up for RFC-175 (router admission).
